description: Prissance is a team driven by curiosity, creativity, and the willingness to turn ideas into reality. As this is our first hackathon, we see it as an opportunity to learn, experiment, challenge ourselves, and grow together. We may be newcomers, but we are ready to think outside the box, embrace challenges, and make the most of this experience. For us, this is just the beginning of something bigger!
summary:
Martian Frontier is an interactive 3D Mars survival simulation designed to make space exploration and planetary science engaging and educational. We developed a game in which players take on the role of an astronaut tasked with surviving seven Martian days (Sols) while managing five essential resources: oxygen, radiation shielding, power, food and communication systems.

Players explore a Martian outpost, operate different facilities, collect research points and make strategic decisions to keep their base functioning. The game also simulates unpredictable Martian weather conditions, including dust storms, heatwaves, radiation storms and extreme cold, requiring players to respond to warnings and seek shelter in a designated bunker.

Our solution addresses the challenge by transforming complex scientific concepts about Mars into an interactive learning experience. Inspired by NASA research and scientific data, Martian Frontier helps players understand the difficulties of establishing human settlements beyond Earth. It is important because it promotes scientific curiosity, problem-solving and awareness of the challenges humanity must overcome to make future Mars exploration possible.
details:
Martian Frontier is an interactive 3D Mars survival simulation that challenges players to survive seven Martian days (Sols) while managing the essential systems of a Martian outpost. Players control an astronaut and explore the base, using different facilities to maintain oxygen, radiation shielding, power, food and communication systems. Each resource gradually decreases, requiring players to make strategic decisions about how to maintain the outpost. The simulation also features dynamic weather events, including dust storms, heatwaves, radiation storms and extreme cold. Players must monitor warnings and seek shelter in the designated bunker to survive. Periodic space quizzes also allow players to test their knowledge and earn research points.

The project provides an engaging way to learn about the scientific and practical challenges of living on Mars. It encourages critical thinking, resource management, problem-solving and scientific curiosity. Our intended impact is to make space science more accessible and inspire interest in planetary exploration and the possibility of future human settlements beyond Earth.

We developed the project as a browser-based application using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with Three.js for the 3D environment and Web Audio API for sound. The project runs offline and does not require specialised hardware.

Its creativity comes from combining a survival game, a 3D exploration experience and educational content in one interactive simulation. We considered scientific relevance, gameplay balance, resource limitations, realistic environmental challenges, user experience and accessibility across different screen sizes. NASA-inspired scientific references, including information associated with NASA DONKI, OSDR, Curiosity RAD and Perseverance MEDA, helped guide the educational content. The weather events themselves are simulated rather than live NASA data.
